108.text: Still, the Christian faith is not a "religion of the book". Christianity is the religion of the "Word" of God, "not a written and mute word, but incarnate and living".[73] If the Scriptures are not to remain a dead letter, Christ, the eternal Word of the living God, must, through the Holy Spirit, ... [rest of sentence not seen verbatim]
108.notes: Footnote 73: St. Bernard, S. missus est hom. 4, 11: PL 183, 86. First two sentences verbatim; third only to 'the Holy'. Used in Ch. 11 line 276 (Redline 22b).
